examples.name: Sample — catastrophe-review-2025_p26
paragraphs: Two charts over the same 55-year axis ticked every third year: event counts on a linear axis (Figure 16) and victims on 1 000 → 10 000 000 decade bands (Figure 17). Each has its own table under its own title, both series across all 55 years — the ticked years by their printed labels, the years between by their axis values (1971, 2023). On the log chart, every value is a band-position estimate to two significant figures, written in the axis's digit grouping, except the two 2024 values, which the side text prints (11 000, 3 200): printed beats geometry, so they are copied. The event callouts and the side text follow the log chart's table as text. Only the first two and last two years of each table are shown.

Source: Caldrivane Institute
Figure 17 Number of victims, 1970 - 2024
Man-made disasters Natural catastrophes
1970 3 000 400 000
1971 2 600 16 000
2023 3 600 70 000
2024 3 200 11 000
1970: Bangladesh storm, Peru earthquake 1976: Tangshan Earthquake, China 1991: Cyclone Gorky, Bangladesh 2004: Indian Ocean Earthquake and tsunami 2008: Cyclone Nargis, Myanmar 2010: Haiti Earthquake 2023: Turkey & Syria earthquake 2024: 11 000 victims from natural catastrophes, below the 2004–2023 annual average. 2024: 3 200 victims from man-made disasters, in line with recent years. Note: Scale is logarithmic: the number of victims increases tenfold per band. Source: Caldrivane Institute
